parts.role: U1. CARRIED VERIFY ITEM #1 SETTLED: cheaper Extended AMS1117-3.3 twins exist in the same SOT-223 package (e.g. C347222 at $0.0484 vs this part's $0.2019), but every Extended MPN adds ONE per-unique-part JLC PCBA setup fee (~$3, decisions.md cost ballpark) on top of unit price. At qty 5 the twin only saves (0.2019-0.0484)x5 = ~$0.77 in unit cost while adding a ~$3 setup fee - a net loss of ~$2.2. Basic C6186 wins decisively; keep it. Governing 0.51W thermal case per ldo-sot223-thermal-copper-sets-current; output cap MUST be tantalum-class per ldo-1117-family-output-cap-esr (see C3).
C2. At U1 VIN on +5V, AFTER the PTC (never ahead of it - Type-C 10uF attach-limit rule). 25V rating gives the DC-bias derating margin power_tree.md assumes (effective ~6-8uF at 5V bias).

alternates.risk: same tantalum family/value, 16V rating, but EIA Case B (3528) vs this part's Case A (3216) - bigger footprint, would need a footprint swap if used

parts.role: C3. LOAD-BEARING per ldo-1117-family-output-cap-esr: the AMS1117 datasheet requires >=22uF SOLID TANTALUM for loop stability (ESR window 0.3-22 ohm per the LM1117 sibling spec) - a bare X5R/X7R ceramic at 22uF has mOhm-level ESR, far below the floor, and is NOT a substitute (this record is GROUNDED for this exact board). This part's 3 ohm@100kHz ESR sits mid-window. No JLC Basic tantalum cap exists at any value (checked live) - Extended is unavoidable for this position. 10V rating = 3x derating over the 3.3V rail (tantalum's own failure mode wants >=2x). Sits on +3V3 behind the LDO, outside the Type-C attach-limit (usbc-sink-attach-capacitance-10uf). CARRIED VERIFY ITEM #3 (SHT4x 20V/ms VDD slew vs AMS1117 startup ramp): the AMS1117 datasheet (downloaded, parts/U1_AMS1117-3.3_C6186.pdf) publishes NO explicit startup/soft-start ramp spec, so the open item from power_tree.md stays open for P4/P8 to verify empirically - not resolved here. What IS confirmed: a tantalum's ESR (ohms) is far higher than a ceramic's (mOhms) at the same capacitance, so this choice, if anything, SLOWS the inrush edge into C3 relative to a same-value ceramic - it does not make the slew-rate risk worse.
D2. Power LED on +3V3 (indicates the rail the logic runs on, decisions.md #11). Vf 1.8-2.4V.

R3. D2 series resistor -> 1.3-2.2mA over the red Vf bin spread (1.8-2.4V), essentially the same operating point as the original 620R design. REVISED per coordinator correction (2026-08-27): 620R has no JLC Basic SKU at any 0402/0603/0805 package (genuine E24 catalog gap, confirmed live); 680R is the adjacent E24 value and IS Basic, so this swap removes an Extended setup fee at essentially zero electrical cost.

C11. Bulk half of the ONE 100nF+4.7uF decoupling pair at U2 pins 4/5 (VDD/VDDA bonded, no separate VREF+) per mcu-decoupling-bonded-vdda-single-pair. C10 (the 100nF half) is the shared C14663 line item above.

R10 (SDA), R11 (SCL). I2C pull-ups at the host (U2), once, per sht4x-i2c-pullup-bus-cap. Value 1.5k unchanged (revised from the P1 2.2k draft at the P2 coverage exit, decisions.md #19). REVISED PACKAGE per coordinator correction (2026-08-27): moved from 0805 to 0603 Basic (same value, same Basic status, same price tier) purely to normalise footprints across the resistor set - see R13 for the same rationale applied board-wide.

R12. D10 series resistor. ELECTRICAL FIX per coordinator correction (2026-08-27), NOT a cost change - do not revert to 220R. D10 is now KT-0805G, Vf 2.6-3.1V against the 3.3V rail: at the original 220R the worst-case bin (Vf 3.1V) gives only (3.3-3.1)/220 = 0.9mA - dim, thin margin the architect flagged in decisions.md #11. At 100R the same worst-case bin gives (3.3-3.1)/100 = 2mA, and the best-case bin (Vf 2.6V) gives (3.3-2.6)/100 = 7mA - 2-7mA across the full bin spread, comfortably visible at the worst corner and well inside the STM32G0 GPIO's 20mA source rating. KEEP AT 100R - P4 should not 'correct' this back toward 220R.

R13. BOOT0 pull-down on PA14/pin 19, POPULATED (decisions.md #20). NORMALISED to 0603 Basic per coordinator's optional suggestion (2026-08-27): after the R10/R11 and R12 swaps, every other resistor on the board (R1/R2, R3, R10/R11, R12) is already 0603, so this was the one remaining 0402 outlier with no functional reason to differ. Took the normalisation - one resistor footprint across the whole BOM, same Basic tier, negligible price delta ($0.0048 vs $0.0019), deep stock (29.8M).

D10. User LED, driven from U2 PA5 through R12 (now 100 ohm - see that entry). Vf 2.6-3.1V typ, 430mcd @5mA. REVISED per coordinator correction (2026-08-27): no JLC Basic green LED exists in 0603 (only red/white are Basic there), but KT-0805G IS Basic in 0805 - package bump costs nothing on this board and removes a setup fee. Power LED D2 stays the Basic red KT-0603R (0603) - two different LED footprints on one board, both Basic, no shared-footprint constraint applies to LEDs.
